title: Cooperative Throttling & Queue Degradation Playbook
body:
Goal:
Design a pragmatic, observable, and incrementally-deployable system for routing backpressure signals through the serving stack and performing admission control per-tenant. This doc collects heuristics, API hooks, config knobs, rollout steps, and experiments (canary + synthetic load) for a cooperative throttling strategy that gracefully degrades queueing and KV cache pressure without global outages.

Context / motivation:
- We've seen multiple incidents where a single noisy tenant or sudden traffic spike caused long tail queueing, huge token costs, and KV cache thrashing. Current hard limits (reject at API gateway) are too blunt; they cause severe UX regressions and make multi-tenant SLOs brittle.
- We want: predictable p95/p99 latency for high-value tenants, fair resource allocation, and controlled graceful degradation for low-value/anonymous traffic.
- This playbook focuses on the scheduler + admission control surface; it also includes recommendations for propagating signals upstream to the API layer and downstream to the runtime kernels (e.g., smaller batch targets, quantized model fallback).

Key principles:
1) Cooperative: propagate soft signals (advice) before hard rejections. API layer, routing, and scheduler should try to reduce load first (smaller batches, shorter seq limits, lower QoS) before returning 429s.
2) Tenant-aware: maintain per-tenant budgets, token buckets, and priority classes. Defaults are fair, but high-paying customers can have reserved headroom.
3) Latency-first for SLAs: for tenants with latency SLOs, prefer shedding throughput vs. increasing service latency.
4) Observability: every decision must emit metrics and an event (why we throttled, which knob was used).
5) Incremental rollout: feature gates per-cluster and canary tenants; start with monitoring-only mode.

High-level flow (request lifecycle):
- API gateway receives request -> checks token-bucket + tenant QoS -> emits "admission-check" event and suggested actions.
- If under soft pressure, API may apply adaptive knobs (reduce max tokens, enable response streaming, attach "queue-priority" header) and forward to scheduler.
- Scheduler (node-level) evaluates global signals: queue depth, head-of-line latency, KV cache hit-rate, GPU occupancy, kernel queue length. It applies admission decisions: immediate dispatch, delayed hold (soft queue), or drop (hard reject).
- When delaying, scheduler assigns a degradation plan to the request (e.g., max_tokens=512, batch_timeout=20ms, allow_quantized_variant).

Admission control primitives and configs:
- tenant_bucket: token bucket per tenant (tokens ~ cost units). Refill rate configurable by plan.
- soft_threshold / hard_threshold: soft triggers for applying degradation vs. hard reject. Soft triggers should be tuned at ~80% of capacity.
- hold_strategy: { FIFO, priority-queue, deadline-aware }. Default = deadline-aware: compute effective deadline = now + client_timeout - safety_margin.
- degradation_profile: list of ordered actions: [reduce_batch_target, reduce_max_tokens, prefer_quantized_model, enable_kv_prefetch_drop, route-to-dedicated-fallback].
- preemptible_slot_count: number of slot units that can be reclaimed from low-priority requests for high-priority ones (soft preemption).
- kv_cache_priority: per-tenant score that influences placement in KV cache eviction.

Signals used for decisioning (metrics):
- node_queue_depth (per backend queue)
- head_of_line_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99)
- kv_cache_hit_rate and kv_eviction_rate
- gpu_utilization and warm_kernel_fraction
- per-tenant token_bucket_level and recent_request_rate
- recent_batch_sizes distribution
- device-level kernel-queue backlog (requests queued inside inference engine)

Decision heuristics (examples):
- If node_queue_depth > soft_threshold and kv_cache_hit_rate < 0.7: apply degradation_profile[0..1] (reduce batch target and max tokens) for low-priority tenants for next 30s. Emit metric "degradation_applied" with reason.
- If head_of_line_latency_p99 increases by > 2x over baseline in 30s: start preemption window. Stop allowing new low-priority admissions and reclaim preemptible_slot_count by cancelling oldest soft-hold requests.
- If per-tenant token_bucket_level drops below 5%: mark tenant as "throttled" and return advisory header X-RINF-Throttle:soft with suggested retry-after. Only escalate to hard 429 if hard_threshold exceeded.

KV cache integration notes:
- Prioritize KV cache for requests we intend to serve with low latency (high-priority tenants). For soft-degraded requests, accept higher KV-miss probability and prefer not to populate cache to avoid thrashing.
- Eviction policy needs tenant-awareness: use an LRU variant weighted by tenant_score * recency. Keep a small protected set for high-paying tenants.
- Expose kv_cache_pressure metric to scheduler; when pressure passes X, scheduler increases preference for short-requests or runs more quantized models.

APIs & headers between layers (proposal):
- X-RINF-Queue-Priority: high|normal|low (used for internal routing)
- X-RINF-Degradation-Plan: json-encoded short plan id (e.g., qp1)
- POST /admit-check (internal) -> returns {allow:bool, plan_id:string, suggested_backoff_ms:int} (for monitoring-only mode, returns allow=true plus recommended actions)
  - For pragmatic reasons we keep the internal admit-check as lightweight HTTP/gRPC call with a small set of fields.

Pseudocode sketch (scheduler decision):
- onRequest(r):
  - look up tenant_bucket; if token_bucket empty -> return reject or suggest retry-after
  - compute deadline = r.deadline or client_timeout - safety
  - if node_queue_depth < soft_threshold -> allow immediate dispatch
  - else if r.priority == high -> try preempt low-priority slots or route to dedicated
  - else -> attach degradation_profile and put into soft-hold queue ordered by earliest deadline

Telemetry and dashboards (must-have):
- Admission decisions per-minute (allow, soft-degrade, reject) by tenant and cluster
- Degradation actions taken (count by type)
- Time in soft-hold queue distribution and % served after hold
- KV cache hit-rate by tenant and by degradation status
- Cost delta metric: estimated tokens saved by degradation actions

Rollout plan:
1) Monitoring-only (2 weeks): implement admit-check path that only logs recommended actions; expose dashboards and alerts.
2) Canary tenants (1 week): enable soft-degrade for 5 small tenants. Measure latency improvements and business impact.
3) Cluster canary (2 weeks): enable across a single cluster with feature flag; limit hard rejects to 1% and keep long backoff windows.
4) Gradual rollout (4-6 weeks): increase coverage, enable preemption, tune thresholds.

Experiments and tests:
- Chaos scenario: synthetic traffic with one tenant doing 10x normal RPS + long tokens. Verify: soft-degrade reduces p99 for protected tenants and cost for noisy tenant.
- KV thrash test: run many small random prefix requests to force eviction; verify that protected tenant hit-rate stays high.
- A/B test: route 50% of similar traffic through new admit-check vs old path; measure p95/p99 and token spend.

Operational runbook (quick):
- Alert: "node_queue_depth > critical" -> set admitting=false at API layer for anonymous tier, escalate to oncall
- Alert: "degradation_applied unexpectedly high" -> look at tenant list producing most degraded requests, contact SEs if customer-facing
- To temporarily disable soft-hold region: flip feature flag on cluster and purge soft-hold queues.

Open questions / tradeoffs (TODO):
- How long should soft-hold survive? Default 30s may be too long for interactive chat but okay for batch summarization. Consider tenant-specific defaults.
- How do we price / communicate degradation to customers? Attach "degraded" metadata to billing/enforcer logs so CS can reason.
- Should kernel-level admission (inside runtime) re-evaluate the plan? Eg. kernel sees high kernel_queue_backlog and can trigger a different action than scheduler planned. We should support feedback loop but guard against oscillation.

Next steps (short list):
- Implement admit-check stub and log-only mode (Asha + Dylan) [INF-3723]
- Add kv_cache_pressure metric and KV tenant-weight config (Miguel)
- Prototype UI for "degradation insights" in console (Priya)
- Write e2e load tests and PoC chaos harness (Liam)

Notes to self / rough TODOs:
- add real Linear/Jira IDs after tickets created
- coordinate with product on messaging and tier defaults
- schedule review with SRE and infra to validate hooks for preemption

Appendix: quick glossary
- soft-hold = delay queue where requests can wait briefly while scheduler tries to reduce load
- soft-degrade = applying non-fatal changes that aim to reduce cost/latency (smaller batches, shorter max tokens, quantized variant)
- hard-reject = immediate 429/403-type response from API indicating admission failure

End of draft.
